title: Titles from /api/shared are inserted as raw HTML
evidence: app.js:46 builds markup from s.title, returned by the server, and passes it to insertAdjacentHTML. No escaping or sanitiser anywhere in app.js or store.js. Traced.
failing_case: Another user shares a note titled . Anyone who types in the search box gets that response, the handler runs in the NoteMaster origin and reads or overwrites every note in localStorage.
remediation: Build the li with createElement and textContent (or one escape function applied at every HTML sink). Add a CSP without 'unsafe-inline'.

title: Note title is interpolated into innerHTML without escaping
evidence: Driven: a stored note with title `` executed on load (window.__x === 1). Also any title containing `<` renders as markup, so a normal title such as `a c` is displayed wrongly.
failing_case: The user names a note `` or pastes such a title from a web page; it runs every render. Combined with any import or sync path it becomes a persistent script injection.
remediation: Create li elements with textContent and dataset, or escape &, <, >, " and ' in one helper at the sink.

title: Delete is an unlabelled div: unreachable by keyboard, no accessible name, invisible until mouse hover, no confirm or undo
evidence: A div with an inline onclick and an emoji as its only content. styles.css:12 sets opacity 0 and reveals it only on li:hover. No button role, no aria-label, no tabindex. removeNote (app.js:23-28) deletes immediately with no confirmation or undo. WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2. Traced.
failing_case: On a phone (no hover) the delete icon never shows. On a keyboard it cannot be focused. With a mouse, a slightly misplaced click on the row's right edge destroys the note permanently, with no way back.
remediation: Use <button type="button" aria-label="Delete note: TITLE"> that is visible on :focus-visible and always on touch screens; add undo (soft delete with a toast) instead of immediate removal.

title: Clicking a shared search result throws and clears the open note
evidence: Shared results are li elements (app.js:46) inside #list, so the list click handler matches them. They have no data-id: Number(undefined) is NaN, notes.find returns undefined, and openNote sets currentNote = undefined (app.js:17) before app.js:18 throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined'. Traced.
failing_case: Type a search term that returns a shared note, click the result. The editor does not change, the console shows a TypeError, and currentNote is now undefined, so further typing hits the timer error from store.js:16 and nothing is saved.
remediation: Give shared rows their own non-clickable markup or handler, and make openNote return early when the id is not found.

title: Viewport blocks pinch zoom
evidence: index.html:5 sets maximum-scale=1. WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA). Traced.
failing_case: A low-vision user on a phone cannot enlarge the page by pinching; Android Chrome honours this, and iOS Safari ignores it by default.
remediation: Use content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1".

title: Title, body and search fields have no accessible name
evidence: index.html:19-20 have no label, aria-label or placeholder; the search input (line 13) relies on a placeholder only. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2 (A). Traced.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'edit text, multiline' for the note title and body; the user cannot tell which is which.
remediation: Add <label for="title">Title</label> and <label for="body">Note</label> (visually hidden if desired) and a label for the search box.

title: Debounced save writes to whatever note is current when the timer fires, and crashes when none is
evidence: Driven: on first run (no notes, currentNote null) typing in #title throws "Cannot set properties of null (setting 'title')" 500 ms later and localStorage stays empty. Traced: the timer closes over the mutable global currentNote, not the note being edited. removeNote sets currentNote = null (app.js:26) and openNote reassigns it (app.js:17).
failing_case: (a) Open note A, type, click note B within 500 ms: openNote replaces the inputs with B's text and sets currentNote to B, then the timer copies B's text onto B; A's edit is lost. (b) Type in a note, then delete it inside 500 ms: currentNote is null when the timer fires and it throws. (c) First run: type into the empty editor; every keystroke ends in a TypeError.
remediation: Capture the target note id and the field values at schedule time (or flush the pending save before openNote/removeNote changes the selection). Guard the null case.

title: Typing with no note selected throws in the timer and silently discards the text
evidence: currentNote starts null (store.js:3). On first run (no notes) the title and body fields are live (index.html:19-20) and their input handler schedules a save. After 500 ms store.js:16 dereferences null: TypeError. The same occurs after removeNote sets currentNote = null (app.js:26) while the old text stays in the editor. Traced.
failing_case: Fresh profile, no notes. The user types a note into the empty editor. The hint 'Changes save automatically' is displayed, but the timer throws 'Cannot read properties of null' in the console and nothing is stored. Reload: the text is gone.
remediation: Disable the editor until a note is open (empty state: 'Create a note to start'), clear and disable it on delete, and guard the timer against a missing target.

title: Write failures (quota, private mode) are swallowed while the UI says changes save automatically
evidence: persist() (store.js:23-27) catches and drops every setItem error. index.html:21 states 'Changes save automatically' unconditionally. No return value, no message. Traced.
failing_case: localStorage is full or blocked (Safari private mode, quota). The user writes a long note, the hint stays unchanged, and on reload everything since the last successful write is gone.
remediation: Return the result of persist(), show a visible error with a next step (export or free space), and keep a 'Saved' or 'Not saved' status that reflects the real outcome.

title: Focus outline removed from all controls with no replacement
evidence: styles.css:6 removes the outline on button, input and textarea. No :focus-visible rule or box-shadow elsewhere in styles.css. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA). Traced.
failing_case: Tab from the search box to 'New note' to the editor fields: nothing shows which control has focus.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px }.

title: Notes can only be opened with a mouse: list items are click-only li elements, not focusable
evidence: Opening happens through a click listener on the ul (app.js:30-33) on plain li elements with no tabindex, role or button. Tab order reaches only the search box, 'New note' and the editor fields. WCAG 2.1.1 (A). Traced.
failing_case: Keyboard-only or screen-reader user with saved notes: after load note 1 is open, but there is no way to switch to any other note. Tab skips the whole list.
remediation: Render each row as a <button> (or li containing one) with an accessible name and aria-current for the open note.

title: Delete is invisible until hover, has no confirm or undo, and is still tappable when invisible
evidence: opacity:0 hides but does not disable the target. removeNote (app.js:23-28) deletes and persists immediately; there is no confirmation or undo. On touch there is no hover, so the control is never visible. Traced from the CSS and handler.
failing_case: On a phone, tap the right end of a note row to open it: the invisible 🗑 sits there and removeNote runs, so the note is deleted and saved to storage without a prompt. On desktop, a mis-click on the same spot does the same.
remediation: Show the control at all times (or on focus-within and hover), make it a labelled button, and either confirm or offer a timed Undo that restores the note.

quote: const sorted = notes.slice().sort((a, b) => b.updated - a.updated);
title: Render sorts the full array once per row and rebuilds the DOM with innerHTML += (quadratic per render)
evidence: Inside shown.forEach (app.js:7) the full copy and sort is repeated for each row, then indexOf (line 9) scans it; list.innerHTML += (line 10) reparses the whole list each iteration. A render runs on every search keystroke. Cost per render is O(n² log n) for the sort and O(n²) for the parsing. Traced.
failing_case: With 500 notes, every keystroke in the search box does 500 sorts of 500 items and 500 full innerHTML reparses of the growing list; the input lags. At 5,000 notes it stalls.
remediation: Sort once before the loop, build a Map of id to rank, and build the list with a single string join or DocumentFragment.

title: The list is not refreshed after an edit: titles and the #rank stay stale
evidence: scheduleSave (store.js:13-21) updates the note and persist()s but never calls renderList. The list is redrawn only by openNote, removeNote and search input. Traced.
failing_case: Rename 'Untitled' to 'Groceries'. The left list still says 'Untitled' and its #rank unchanged until the user clicks another note or types in search.
remediation: Re-render (or update the one row) after the save fires, preserving the current search filter.

title: Out-of-order search responses are appended to the list, and every keystroke sends the query
evidence: Each input event synchronously re-renders local results, then fires an unthrottled fetch; each response appends to whatever is on screen. No AbortController, no sequence check, no res.ok check (a 404 HTML page throws in res.json and is only console.log'd). openNote or removeNote also call renderList, which wipes shared rows silently. Traced.
failing_case: Type 'ab' quickly. Request for 'a' and request for 'ab' are in flight; the render for 'ab' has already cleared the list. Responses arrive in either order and both sets of shared rows are appended, so stale results for 'a' appear under 'ab', often twice. Every keystroke also sends the partial search text to the server with no consent step.
remediation: Debounce the request, abort the previous one, ignore responses whose query is not the current value, check res.ok, and render shared results from state in the same render pass.

title: First run shows a blank list and an editable editor that cannot save
evidence: Driven: with empty storage no note is selected, the list is empty with no text, and #title and #body are live. Typing there throws 500 ms later (see store.js:16) and nothing is stored, while the hint says 'Changes save automatically'.
failing_case: A new user opens the page, sees nothing telling them to press New note, and starts typing. Everything typed is lost.
remediation: Show 'No notes yet. Press New note to start.' in the list, disable the editor until a note is open, and select the first note after delete.

title: Unguarded JSON.parse of saved notes bricks the whole app on bad or wrong-shaped data
evidence: Driven in Chromium. With localStorage notes set to '{bad', store.js throws at load, so `notes` is never defined, and app.js then throws 'notes is not defined'; the list is empty and nothing works. With notes set to '{}' (valid JSON, not an array) load succeeds but renderList throws 'notes.filter is not a function'. Every reload repeats it.
failing_case: Storage holds a truncated write, a hand edit, or another app's value for the key 'notes' ('{bad' or '{}'). The user opens the page: blank list, dead New button, no message. The only way out is clearing site data in devtools, which also deletes whatever notes were recoverable.
remediation: Load inside try/catch, check Array.isArray and each record's fields, copy the raw string to a backup key before falling back to [], and show the user a recovery message. Add a schema version to the saved shape.

title: No flush on pagehide or unload: the last 500 ms of typing is lost
evidence: The only writer for edits is the debounce timer (store.js:13-21). There is no pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload listener anywhere in the payload. Traced.
failing_case: Type a sentence and close the tab or refresh within half a second. The timer never fires and the sentence is not stored.
remediation: On pagehide and visibilitychange (hidden), clear the timer and run the save synchronously.

title: Fixed 1200px container makes the page scroll sideways on phones and at zoom
evidence: width:1200px (not max-width) plus a 300px + 1fr grid (styles.css:7) has no media query. At 390 px or 200%/400% zoom the layout is wider than the viewport. WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA).
failing_case: At 390 px width the page is about 3x the viewport; the editor sits off-screen and the user must pan sideways to see it.
remediation: Use `width: 100%; max-width: 1200px; box-sizing: border-box` and a single-column grid under about 700px.

title: Hint, rank numbers and input borders are far below contrast minimums
evidence: Computed with the WCAG formula: #ccc on #fff 1.61:1 (styles.css:15, needs 4.5:1); #bbb rank text on #fff 1.92:1 and on the active row #eef 1.67:1 (styles.css:11, 10); #eee input border on #fff 1.16:1 (styles.css:13, needs 3:1 under 1.4.11); white paragraph text on the #8b5cf6 end of the hero gradient 4.23:1 (styles.css:3, needs 4.5:1); the white-on-#6366f1 button text is 4.47:1, just under 4.5. WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 (AA).
failing_case: A user with low vision, or anyone in daylight, cannot read the hint or rank, and cannot see where the text fields begin.
remediation: Use text colours of at least #595959 on white, a field border of at least #767676, and darker brand violet (for example #4f46e5) for button and hero backgrounds.

title: Deleting a note drops the active search filter, and the editor keeps showing the deleted note
evidence: removeNote (app.js:23-28) calls renderList() with no argument while #search still holds text, so the list shows all notes under a filled search box. When the open note is deleted, currentNote is nulled but title and body fields are not cleared (app.js:26). Traced.
failing_case: Search 'milk', delete one match: every note reappears while the box still says 'milk'. Delete the open note: its text stays in the editor as though still saved.
remediation: Pass document.getElementById('search').value to renderList, and clear and disable the editor when the open note is removed.

quote:
✨ Welcome to NoteMaster

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, your notes, supercharged.
title: Placeholder copy shipped in the hero: Lorem ipsum, 'Welcome to...', emoji, marketing tagline
evidence: index.html:11. The hero banner (styles.css:3: indigo-to-violet gradient, 16 px radius, 60 px padding) pushes the toolbar and editor down by about 200 px; Inter font stack (styles.css:1) without an @font-face or link, so the fallback is shown. These match ai-tells.md (stock palette, 'Welcome to', lorem ipsum). No recorded decision asked for them.
failing_case: A user opening the app first reads 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' as the product's description.
remediation: Remove the hero or reduce it to a plain title. Write real copy (what the app does) and choose a palette and type for the product.

title: Date.now() ids collide, and delete removes every note with the same id
evidence: createNote (store.js:6-11) uses the millisecond clock as id. deleteNote (store.js:29-32) filters by id; openNote (app.js:17) uses find, which returns the first match. Traced.
failing_case: Double-click 'New note' (or press Enter twice on the focused button): two notes get the same id in the same millisecond. Clicking the second row opens the first. Deleting either removes both, with the text of the second lost.
remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a counter persisted with the notes. Ignore a second create in the same tick.
